kurals.tr: Nanmaiyum Theemaiyum Naati Nalampurindha / Thanmaiyaan Aalap Patum
kurals.m: He should be employed (by a king), whose nature leads him to choose the good, after having weighed both the evil and the good in any undertaking

kurals.tr: Vaari Perukki Valampatuththu Utravai / Aaraaivaan Seyka Vinai
kurals.m: Let him do (the king's) work who can enlarge the sources (of revenue), increase wealth and considerately prevent the accidents (which would destroy it)

kurals.tr: Anparivu Thetram Avaavinmai Innaankum / Nankutaiyaan Katte Thelivu
kurals.m: Let the choice (of a king) fall upon him who largely possesses these four things, love, knowledge, a clear mind and freedom from covetousness

kurals.tr: Enaivakaiyaan Theriyak Kannum Vinaivakaiyaan / Veraakum Maandhar Palar
kurals.m: Even when (a king) has tried them in every possible way, there are many men who change, from the nature of the works (in which they may be employed)

kurals.tr: Arindhaatrich Cheykirpaarku Allaal Vinaidhaan / Sirandhaanendru Evarpaar Randru
kurals.m: (A king's) work can only be accomplished by a man of wisdom and patient endurance; it is not of a nature to be given to one from mere personal attachment

kurals.tr: Seyvaanai Naati Vinainaatik Kaalaththotu / Eydha Unarndhu Seyal
kurals.m: Let (a king) act, after having considered the agent (whom he is to employ), the deed (he desires to do), and the time which is suitable to it

kurals.tr: Ithanai Ithanaal Ivanmutikkum Endraaindhu / Adhanai Avankan Vital
kurals.m: After having considered, "this man can accomplish this, by these means", let (the king) leave with him the discharge of that duty

kurals.tr: Vinaik Kurimai Naatiya Pindrai / Avanai Adharkuriya Naakach Cheyal
kurals.m: Having considered what work a man is fit for, let (the king) employ him in that work

kurals.tr: Vinaikkan Vinaiyutaiyaan Kenmaive Raaka / Ninaippaanai Neengum Thiru
kurals.m: Prosperity will leave (the king) who doubts the friendship of the man who steadily labours in the discharge of his duties

kurals.tr: Naatorum Naatuka Mannan Vinaiseyvaan / Kotaamai Kotaa Thulaku
kurals.m: Let a king daily examine the conduct of his servants; if they do not act crookedly, the world will not act crookedly
